title: Hotfix: prevent rollout UI from rendering internal-only model release notes for non-admin roles
author: Felix Schneider
release_notes: - Security: Internal-only release note fields are no longer rendered in Console for non-admin roles (defense-in-depth).
description:
Context: During the rollouts UI dogfood of the new model change history / release notes surfaces, we found a case where internal-only note fields (e.g. `internal_summary`, `internal_risk_assessment`, and links to internal runbooks) could appear in the Console for standard (non-admin) roles. This is not expected and violates the public/internal separation we agreed on in ENG-9825.

Root cause: The Rollouts `ReleaseNotesCard` component was rendering the `details` payload verbatim when present. Under certain navigation paths (rollout timeline -> "Change details" -> "Release notes"), the UI was using an internal-capable response type and the renderer did not gate the internal sections on RBAC. While the backend should also enforce this (and does for the public feed), the UI should not trust the presence of fields.

Fix (hotfix / defense-in-depth): (1) Gate all internal-only sections in the Console renderer behind an explicit `canViewInternalReleaseNotes` permission check; (2) add a safe "public projection" mapping that drops all `internal_*` fields by default before rendering; (3) add a regression test that logs in as a standard role and asserts internal-only copy never appears, even when the API response contains internal fields.

Notes: This PR intentionally stays scoped to Console UI + its local API client typing. Follow-up work to further harden the backend response shaping is tracked separately (ENG-9864) but not required for the immediate leak.

Rollout plan: Merge ASAP, deploy with the next Console hotfix train. No schema changes.

Risk: Low. Changes are additive and limited to UI rendering + tests.

Checklist: - [x] Added regression coverage - [x] Verified in staging with standard role + admin role - [x] Confirmed no user-visible copy changes for public release notes
commits: console: add RBAC-gated internal release notes rendering
console: public projection for release note details payload
tests: add regression test to prevent internal notes leakage

conversation:
Jada Williams (review): The projection helper is a good idea. Can we make the deny-by-default behavior obvious? I want to avoid future components accidentally rendering internal fields.

Felix Schneider (author): Yep. I renamed the helper to `projectReleaseNotesPublicView()` and made the default export the public projection. Internal view now requires calling `projectReleaseNotesInternalView()` explicitly and passing `canViewInternalReleaseNotes=true`.

Marcus Lin (review): Please confirm we don’t render internal runbook links or eval IDs in any non-admin path. Also, can we ensure we don’t leave internal fields in the DOM as hidden text (e.g. aria-only or display:none)?

Felix Schneider (author): Confirmed. The internal blocks are not mounted at all unless `canViewInternalReleaseNotes` is true. Cypress asserts the strings are absent from the DOM and also checks for known internal URL patterns (`go/redwood/*`).

Chloe Martin (review): The component is used in two contexts (rollout timeline and model history drawer). Did you validate both?

Felix Schneider (author): Yes. Added coverage for the rollout timeline path in Cypress and verified the model history drawer manually in staging with a standard role.

Kenji Nakamura (design): Any visual changes for public users?

Felix Schneider (author): None intended. Public users only lose the (incorrectly visible) "Internal notes" accordion. Public sections unchanged.

Jada Williams (approval): Looks good. Please add a short comment near the renderer explaining why we project fields instead of trusting API shape.

Felix Schneider (author): Added comment in `releaseNotesProjection.ts` referencing ENG-9825 and the public/internal contract.

Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Defense-in-depth is the right call for hotfix.

Merge: Squash and merge after green CI.
